purpose: Record scale compliance separately from owner-rejected aesthetics: the candidate pixels remain source-only until morphology, cutout, color grouping, and shared finish pass review.

anchor.role: owner-approved scale and pixel-cluster finish reference only; identity, costume and palette are not borrowed by other characters

explicit_owner_constraints: Golden Axe Warrior is no taller than Alis.
Dr. Social reads at least as large as Joe Musashi while remaining lean.
Landau keeps the approved character design while matching the roster pixel-art production finish of Hayato.
Alis and J.J. must not read as chibi.
All roster sprites must be reviewed together for scale, style and morphology.
Use Joe Musashi as the lean human morphology reference, not as a source of edge or palette defects.
Make head/face, torso/waist and limbs read as human proportions; avoid squat bodies, oversized heads and thickened limbs.
Separate correct palette entries from palette use: coherent material clusters, no dithering, halo, or decorative color speckles.
A common roster board must include recorded visual outcomes for morphology, clean cutout, palette grouping and shared finish.
derived_working_targets_note: Pixel bands are reviewable working targets inferred from the measured Hayato sprite and owner constraints; they are not hardware limits. Width measures the opaque outer silhouette including hair, cape, weapon and shield, so it screens visual occupancy and never replaces a human body-proportion review.
width_measurement_note: The measured width includes all visible equipment and hair. Use width relations as a coarse perceived-size screen; judge torso/limb build and chibi read in the common review board.
visual_standard: One common baseline and native sprite scale; nearest-neighbor enlargement is presentation only.
Use each source game for identity and palette values; no character borrows another character’s colors.
Hayato is the finish/cluster reference; Joe is the lean body-proportion reference. These authorities are separate.
Check human head/face, torso/waist and limb mass; avoid stocky/chibi reads and wide limbs unless the approved concept requires them.
Keep exact SMS palette entries but group them by material with deliberate base/shadow/highlight clusters; no dithering, halo or color speckles.
Inspect cutout edges at native size and 4x nearest-neighbor on light and dark backgrounds; run resource and material-region audits where defined.
Record pass/fail/pending separately for identity/palette, anatomy, cutout, color grouping, shared finish and native readability.
A dimension pass never approves identity, visual style, animation, resource integration or ROM.

revision_note_2026_10_04: The owner accepted the common scale comparison and generally correct palette values, but rejected this aesthetic proposal: Joe cutout dirt; stocky/chibi morphology in other characters; and color-cluster/finish pollution. New review axes are mandatory. Scale bands and sprite pixels remain unchanged in this review record.

morphology_anchor.role: owner-designated reference for lean human head/torso/limb proportions and fighter mass only; do not copy its cutout/edge defects, costume, palette or rendering finish

accepted_axes: palette values are generally on direction
observations: Joe Musashi has visible dirt/halo around the cutout; prior clean-edge lessons did not prevent regression.
Other roster figures read stocky/chibi, with overly wide limbs and less convincing human head/face proportions than Joe.
Keep the declared Master System palette values, but regroup color into quieter coherent material clusters; some conversions read color-polluted.
The earlier concepts had stronger painting/cluster quality; palette conversion must preserve that clarity rather than add noise.
owner_review.revision_direction: Use Joe only as a lean-morphology reference and Hayato only as a pixel-finish reference. Revise original sprite source on the native grid; do not fix anatomy by whole-sprite scaling.
